situation: Checking a Guest in on the day
given: a confirmed Reservation whose first night is the Property's business date, on a ready Unit nobody is in
when: a Staff Member holding front_desk.check_in presses Check in
then: one transaction: the Reservation becomes checked_in, one in_house Stay is created from it, the Folio is opened where the Property bills, stay.checked_in is published and reservation.checked_in is audited naming the actor at the Property. Blueprint 6.1 and 7.4; PR #29, #31, commit eeb3425

situation: TIME — arriving before the first night
given: a confirmed Reservation whose first night is after the business date
then: refused with CheckInError and nothing is written. The module refuses on its date predicate and stays_insert_front_desk refuses an in_house Stay starting after app.property_today() independently, on both the insert and the update path, so a reserved Stay cannot be moved in house early either. PR #31, commit 9331313, 20260916001300

situation: TIME — a late arrival inside the booking
given: a confirmed Reservation that began two days ago and still has nights left
when: the Guest arrives and is checked in
then: allowed. The Stay starts on the business date they actually arrived, not the planned one, and the nights they missed are not held by the Stay. PR #31 (the Stay starts on the actual arrival date), commit 9331313

situation: TIME — arriving on the day the booking ends
given: a confirmed Reservation whose ends_on is the business date
then: refused: no night is left, and a Stay of [today, today) would hold no Unit. The module requires ends_on > today and stays_in_house_has_a_night refuses the row for every role, the migration role included. Commit 3340579

situation: TIME — arriving after the booking ended
given: a confirmed Reservation whose last night has already passed
then: refused with CheckInError; the row has also left the arrivals list (CI-S3-03), so this is reached only from a stale screen. PR #31, commit 610929e

situation: TIME — past midnight, before the cutoff
given: a one-night Reservation for last evening and a Guest landing at 00:30, with the Property's cutoff at 04:00
then: allowed: the business date is still last evening's, so the Reservation is dated for today and the Stay starts on that business date. Every check-in date comparison goes through app.property_today(). ADR 0021, amended 2026-09-22

situation: TIME — before the cutoff, for a booking dated the new calendar day
given: a Reservation starting on the 5th and a Guest arriving at 02:00 on the 5th, with the cutoff at 04:00
then: refused as an early arrival until the cutoff passes, because the business date is still the 4th. This follows from ADR 0021's rule, but no source addresses this case and no test exercises it

situation: A walk-in
given: a Guest with no booking at the desk
when: the desk wants them in a room now
then: the only path today is to take a booking starting today (createReservation accepts today's date) and then check it in. Nothing creates a Stay without a Reservation. No source states this as the walk-in flow; see CI-NB-01

situation: An open-ended Resident
given: a confirmed Reservation with no ends_on
then: the Stay has no end and holds the Unit from arrival onwards (ADR 0033); a later confirmed booking on that Unit makes the check-in refuse with 55006, because app.stay_holds() gives an open-ended Stay every night. The booking-side rule is FD-S2-04; the check-in side has no test

situation: Checking in over somebody else's booking
given: another confirmed Reservation holds tonight on the Unit
when: a Stay would go in house over it
then: refused with 55006 (object in use), surfaced as UnitHasOccupantError: a Stay may not take nights another confirmed booking holds. ADR 0033

situation: CONCURRENCY — two desks, one Reservation
given: one confirmed Reservation on two screens
when: both desks press Check in at once, or one presses it again
then: one Stay and one refusal. The Reservation's row lock re-evaluates status = 'confirmed' for the second caller, and the unique index on reservation_id (partial: status <> 'cancelled') makes two live Stays for one Reservation unrepresentable. The second desk gets the generic refusal. 20260916001000, ADR 0022 amended

situation: ACCESS — another Organization's Reservation
given: a Reservation id from an Organization the Staff Member does not belong to
then: refused, and the row is unchanged. Whether the answer is identical to one for a Reservation that does not exist is not asserted

situation: ACCESS — a Resident checks themselves in
given: a Resident signed in to the Portal with their own Reservation
when: they try to write their Stay in house
then: refused: the write policies resolve through organization membership and a Stay is not one. ADR 0009

situation: ACCESS — a Property the Staff Member is not assigned to
given: a Staff Member with assigned_properties reach and a Reservation at an unassigned Property of their Organization
then: refused like a Reservation that does not exist: app.can_use_capability() carries reach, so the Reservation's update matches no row. No check-in test isolates reach; CO-S1-09 is the check-out counterpart

situation: ACCESS — commercial gates
given: the Organization's Subscription is suspended, its front_office Entitlement is revoked, or front_desk is off at the Property
then: refused by matching nothing: both the Reservation update and the Stay insert policies call app.can_use_capability(). The nearest test is the Reservation-update gate test, which uses a cancel; whether a suspended Organization should still check Guests in is CO-S4-02, which is still open

situation: The arrival is published
given: a check-in that commits
then: exactly one stay.checked_in is in the outbox from the same transaction, carrying ids and no Guest name, because the queue is read across Organizations. ADR 0017, commit eeb3425

situation: Dirty and occupied at once
given: a stale arrivals row for a Unit that is both not ready and has somebody in it
then: the desk is asked about readiness first, because checkIn tests readiness before inserting the Stay; after Check in anyway it is refused as occupied. Nothing is written either time. Code order only, with no source and no test

situation: A check-in fails unexpectedly
given: a lost connection or a schema error, not a refusal the module raised
then: checkInReservation logs it with console.error and shows the generic refusal, unlike a CheckInError, which is not logged. PR #39 states this rule for withdrawal only, and nothing tests it for check-in

situation: REVERSAL — withdrawing a mistaken check-in
given: an in_house Stay from a check-in with nothing posted to its Folio
when: a Staff Member holding front_desk.check_in withdraws it with a reason
then: the Stay becomes cancelled, keeping its dates and reservation_id; the Reservation returns to confirmed; the Unit is free again. Nothing is deleted and the Stay is never edited back to reserved. ADR 0022

situation: REVERSAL — the reason
given: a withdrawal whose trimmed reason is under 3 or over 2000 characters
then: refused before anything moves; the bounds are the audit column's, published as REVERSAL_REASON. ADR 0022 and blueprint 7.4; PR #39

situation: MONEY — charges have been posted
given: an in_house Stay whose Folio carries a line
then: refused with 55000 by stays_withdrawal_is_free_of_charges, surfaced as StayHasChargesError, and both rows stay exactly as they were: this is now a stay that happened, and correcting it is a credit or refund (blueprint 5.9). ADR 0022

situation: MONEY — charges the withdrawer cannot see
given: a Staff Member holding front_desk and not finance
when: they withdraw a check-in whose Folio carries a line
then: still refused: the trigger is security definer, so it does not depend on folio_lines staying reach-readable. ADR 0022 states and argues this; no test pins the definer, and the pgTAP header says its own assertions cannot prove it

situation: CONCURRENCY — a withdrawal and a charge at once
given: one connection posting a charge while another withdraws the check-in
then: never a withdrawn Stay carrying money: both triggers take the Stay's advisory lock (namespace 1) before checking, so the second waits and then re-reads. Write skew reproduced before the fix. ADR 0022, commit 3340579

situation: MONEY — nothing posts after a withdrawal
given: a Stay that was withdrawn
when: any role, the migration role included, posts a line to its Folio
then: refused by folio_line_is_postable(). ADR 0022

situation: MONEY — the empty Folio is closed
given: a check-in that opened a Folio and is then withdrawn
when: the withdrawal commits, and the Reservation is later checked in again
then: closeEmptyFolioWithin closes the first Folio in the withdrawal's own transaction and the second check-in opens a new one, so the Reservation has exactly one open Folio. Both Folios remain. ADR 0022 amended, PR #35

situation: MONEY — a Folio with a line is never closed as empty
given: an open Folio on a cancelled Stay that carries a line (unreachable now; possible in older databases)
when: the 20260916001900 backfill runs, or closeEmptyFolioWithin is called
then: refused and left exactly as it was, so somebody can decide on a credit or a refund. A migration does not get to decide that. ADR 0022, PR #35

situation: REVERSAL — withdrawn twice
given: a check-in already withdrawn
then: refused with the generic refusal rather than reported as success. PR #39, landed via #42

situation: REVERSAL — a withdrawal cannot become a room move
given: a withdrawal that also names another Unit
then: refused with 42501: the column grant on stays covers (status, ends_on, updated_at) and not accommodation_unit_id. ADR 0022, Consequences

situation: The withdrawal is audited and published
given: a withdrawal that commits
then: reservation.check_in_reversed is audited with the actor, the reason, the Property and the stayId, and stay.check_in_reversed follows stay.checked_in in the outbox, in the same transaction. ADR 0022

situation: REVERSAL — on a later business date
given: a check-in from an earlier business date with nothing posted
then: allowed: neither the module nor the database bounds the command by date, only by money (ADR 0022: the window closes when money exists). Only the arrivals screen limits it to the day (CI-S3-01). No test

situation: INTERFACE — a late arrival checked in today
given: a Guest due yesterday and checked in this morning
then: the row stays for the rest of the day, carrying its stayId and not offering Check in again, because a Stay that began today is a second way onto the list. That is where the check-in is withdrawn. ADR 0022 amended 2026-09-17, commit 37f90f2

situation: INTERFACE — after the withdrawal
given: that row's check-in withdrawn
then: the row is confirmed and offers Check in, and stayId is null, so the screen cannot offer to withdraw it twice. ADR 0022

situation: INTERFACE — what the arrivals list holds
given: a Guest checked in months ago, and a booking whose nights all passed unused
then: neither is listed: a late arrival stays only while check-in would still accept them, and today's Reservations stay all day. Commit 610929e

situation: INTERFACE — the button agrees with the command
given: every kind of arrivals row
when: the list is read and check-in is pressed on each
then: canCheckIn is true exactly where checkIn succeeds; the flag is the command's predicate, not a restatement of it. Commit 610929e

situation: INTERFACE — checking in from the screen
given: a confirmed arrival on the arrivals screen
when: Check in is pressed in a browser
then: the button is on the row, reaches the server action, and the row reads Checked in. PR #38

situation: INTERFACE — undo is offered where it may fail
given: a checked-in row whose Stay has charges
when: the desk opens undo and submits a reason
then: the control is offered on every row naming an in-house Stay, and the refusal says charges were posted and to correct them in Finance. Asking a component would be the weaker check and would hide the one refusal a desk can act on. PR #39, landed via #42

situation: INTERFACE — the charges message
given: a withdrawal refused for charges
when: it is shown in each locale
then: a message of its own, never the generic refusal, translated in all three languages. PR #39

situation: INTERFACE — every other refusal
given: a withdrawal refused for being out of reach, already departed, already withdrawn or never having happened
then: one message: That check-in cannot be withdrawn. Telling them apart would confirm that a Stay exists. PR #39

situation: INTERFACE — an error that is not a refusal
given: reverseCheckIn fails with an error the module never raised
then: undoOutcomeFor answers null; the action logs it and only then reports refused, so a lost connection is recorded and not read as normal. PR #39

situation: INTERFACE — the reason field's bounds
given: the undo dialog
when: somebody types past 2000 characters, or submits too few
then: typing stops at the module's own maximum, and a short or long reason gets a message about the field that names the bound, in ICU for all three languages. PR #39

situation: INTERFACE — a reason of spaces
given: three spaces typed as the reason
then: refused as too short, because the trimmed string is what is stored, and what was typed stays in the field; it is forgotten when the dialog is dismissed. Commit 75bb921, PR #39

situation: INTERFACE — focus after a withdrawal
given: a withdrawal submitted from the keyboard
then: focus lands on that row's Check in button, not the document body. Commit 65ad5ef, PR #39

situation: INTERFACE — the Guest's name inside Arabic
given: a Latin Guest name such as Ada Lovelace (VIP) in the undo control
when: it is rendered in Arabic, Turkish or English
then: the name is isolated with <bdi> in the dialog and with U+2068/U+2069 in the aria-label, so bidi does not reorder it against the words around it. PR #39

situation: INTERFACE — the not-ready question at a desk
given: a not-ready room on the arrivals list at 1440x900
when: Check in is pressed and the question appears
then: the warning and its two buttons, stacked, fit the row with no horizontal overflow. PR #69

situation: INTERFACE — another desk checks somebody in
given: the arrivals screen open on two terminals
when: one of them checks a Guest in
then: the other's list shows it on the next poll, every 30 seconds, paused while the tab is hidden. ADR 0019 sets 30–60 seconds; departures polls the same way (FD-S5-05). No test covers the arrivals interval

situation: INTERFACE — the arrivals read with no session or a bad Property
given: a poll with no session, or with a missing or malformed Property id
then: 401 with no body without a session; a bad or missing id is answered as an empty day, never as an error that reveals anything. ADR 0019

situation: INTERFACE — an empty arrivals list
given: a Property in another Organization, or a Staff Member of another Organization
then: nothing of it is shown: the read's own query carries the gates (ADR 0012), so the screen is the same empty day as a quiet one. The no-Entitlement case, the quiet day and the No arrivals today copy are not asserted here

situation: INTERFACE — a refused poll
given: an arrivals poll answered 401 (the route answers nothing else; a Property out of reach comes back as an empty day)
then: ADR 0019 says clear the relevant queries and show the uniform message; live-arrivals.tsx keeps the last good rows on screen instead, so a signed-out desk goes on seeing Guests' names and a Check in button that will be refused

situation: A walk-in as a Stay of its own
given: a Guest with no Reservation
when: the desk wants to check them straight in
then: open: nothing creates a Stay without a Reservation (module.ts, which calls it not reachable yet), and no source decides whether a walk-in is a booking-then-check-in (CI-S1-08) or a Stay without a Reservation. RC-NB-02 leaves it out of the room calendar's scope

situation: Withdrawing a Stay that had no Reservation
given: an in_house Stay with no reservation_id (only a test can create one today)
then: refused with the generic refusal: there is no Reservation to return, and ending such a Stay is a check-out. This is the module's rule; no source states it and no test covers it

situation: An early arrival the desk wants to take
given: a Guest who arrives a day before their Reservation starts
when: the desk wants them in tonight
then: deferred: check-in refuses (CI-S1-02), and moving a booking's dates is not built. The roadmap says nothing amends or moves a booking

situation: Legal registration and identity at arrival
given: a Property in Türkiye, where arriving Guests are reported to a public system
then: deferred: nothing records identity documents or notifies a public system. Blueprint 6.6 says a check-in must not bypass legal registration or identity verification, and the Türkiye section lists public-system integrations. The roadmap has no row for either; CO-S1-33 defers the departure notification to compliance

situation: Something acting on an arrival
given: stay.checked_in in the outbox
then: deferred: no handler consumes it, and that is a position. Every candidate — a confirmation, a room charge — needs a workflow that does not exist (commit eeb3425, apps/worker/src/outbox/subscriptions.ts)

situation: A mistaken check-in noticed the next day
given: a check-in made on an earlier business date
when: the desk looks for it to withdraw it
then: deferred: it is not on arrivals, and is not meant to be. Blueprint 18.6's Reservation timeline is where it would be reached, and that is not built (ADR 0022, roadmap timeline row). The command itself would still accept it (CI-S2-14)
